The Korean keyboard does not ask you to: The Korean keyboard does not ask you to type a romanized spelling. It gives each physical key a Hangul letter. On the standard 2-set layout, called 두벌식 (dubeolsik), the left side is mostly consonants and the right side is vowels. Press the letters in spoken syllable order and the input method combines them into square Hangul blocks.

The strongest shortcut is to learn zones: The strongest shortcut is to learn zones before individual keys. Your left hand supplies the consonant frame of a syllable: the opening sound and, when present, the final consonant. Your right hand supplies the vowel in the middle. A simple block such as 한 therefore moves left–right–left: ㅎ on G, ㅏ on K, ㄴ on S.
The top row contains the letters that re: The top row contains the letters that require Shift as well as several common vowels. The home row carries high-frequency letters such as ㄴ, ㅇ, ㄹ, ㅏ, ㅓ, ㅗ, and ㅣ. The bottom row contains the aspirated consonants ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅊ, ㅍ and the vowels ㅠ, ㅜ, ㅡ. Learning those row patterns makes recall faster than studying twenty-six unrelated pairs.
